# 15 — Safety and Scope Boundary

## 1. Allowed Research Targets

* Synthetic semiprimes generated by this laboratory;
* Historical, public RSA challenge numbers (e.g. RSA-100, RSA-110, RSA-250);
* Deliberately structured synthetic controls (Family F, Family P1);
* Published benchmark instances from the scientific literature.

---

## 2. Excluded Operational Behavior

The project strictly does not:
* Crawl or scan the internet or network interfaces for RSA public keys or certificates;
* Attempt to recover private keys belonging to deployed, live third-party systems;
* Automate cyber-offensive exploitation or unauthorized key extraction;
* Use recovered factor values to access unauthorized systems or data.

---

## 3. Scientific Rationale

Synthetic and historical challenge numbers are superior scientific material:
* Ground truth is fully controlled;
* Modulus distributions and prime properties are mathematically reproducible;
* Sealed holdout partitions prevent data contamination;
* Empirical scaling can be isolated from operational noise.

---

## 4. Breakthrough Boundary

If an algorithm or search branch unexpectedly succeeds at factoring substantially larger balanced-random semiprimes, execution halts immediately under the **Breakthrough Protocol** (see [11_LONG_RUN_AND_STOPPING.md](11_LONG_RUN_AND_STOPPING.md)). The code does not pivot to live targets.
